title: Answer to Question: America's Announcement of Its Plan to Sell Weapons to Taiwan
text:
Answer to Question: America's Announcement of Its Plan to Sell Weapons to Taiwan

Question:

On 29/1/2010 it was announced that the Obama administration had informed the American Congress of its plan to sell weapons to Taiwan worth 6.4 billion dollars, including anti-missile missiles, helicopters, minesweeper ships and communication equipment for F-16 fighter aircraft.

So what is America's benefit from the arms deal with Taiwan? And how does America risk its relations with China, which supported it relatively at the time of the economic crisis, in addition to what had appeared to be an improvement in relations between America and China, especially after Obama's arrival and especially his visit to China in November 2009 CE? And does Taiwan have importance for America after America abandoned its recognition of it as the representative of China? Or are there other aims behind the matter? We ask you to clarify this, and may Allah reward you with good.

Answer:

1- Yes, the Obama administration, as stated in the question, informed Congress on 29/1/2010 CE of its plan to sell weapons to Taiwan worth 6.4 billion dollars, including anti-missile missiles, helicopters, minesweeper ships and communication equipment for F-16 fighter aircraft...

In the wake of that... the Chinese reaction came disturbed and severely angry. The Chinese Deputy Foreign Minister He Yafei announced China's strong reaction, issuing a statement in which he warned that this American project of selling weapons to Taiwan “will undoubtedly harm Chinese-American relations, and will have negative and serious repercussions on exchanges and cooperation between the two countries in major fields.” He added: “This new American step of selling weapons to Taiwan, which forms an inseparable part of China, is a blatant interference in internal affairs, exposes Chinese national security to grave danger and undermines the efforts aimed at reunifying the country peacefully.” “A strongly worded protest has been sent to the American ambassador in Beijing.” (China's “Xinhua” page, 30/1/2010). Then the Chinese Foreign Minister Yang Jiechi expressed his country's firm position towards American arms sales to Taiwan, saying: “The United States, in blatant disregard of the strong opposition and repeated Chinese protest, has announced its plan to sell weapons to Taiwan worth 6.4 billion dollars.” He said: “This step flagrantly contradicts the three joint communiqués between China and the United States, especially the communiqué of 17 August.” He added that this constitutes a crude interference in China's internal affairs and harms China's national security and the efforts to reunify it peacefully. He demanded that America immediately cancel the wrong decision relating to this deal, respect China's core interests and respect the United States' commitment to supporting the peaceful growth of relations across the Taiwan Strait. (The same source.) Likewise, the Chinese Ministry of Defence and the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Chinese People's Congress issued similar strongly worded statements in protest at the American arms deal with Taiwan. Besides that, China took practical steps connected to its protest: a press statement was issued by the Chinese Foreign Ministry saying: “China has decided to partially suspend the programmes of exchanges between the armies of the two countries, as well as the consultations at the level of deputy ministers on strategic security, arms control and non-proliferation which had originally been scheduled to be held soon.” It said: “China will also impose sanctions on the American companies involved in arms sales to Taiwan.” And it stated: “Chinese-American cooperation on major regional and international issues will inevitably be affected because of that issue.” (Xinhua, 30/1/2010).

2- This is with regard to China's reactions and their striking heat. As for America, its reaction to the Chinese reactions was cold and indifferent: none of the senior officials in the American administration said anything, and this administration sufficed with a statement by a spokeswoman for its State Department, Laura Tischler, in which she said: “Such sales contribute to maintaining security and stability across the Taiwan Strait. And they are consistent with the American 'One China' policy and the Taiwan Relations Act, and are likewise consistent with the three Chinese-American joint communiqués that guide relations between the two states.” (Reuters, 30/1/2010). This is despite the fact that the American action does indeed contradict the three communiqués, especially the communiqué of 17 August in which the United States pledged not to seek to carry out long-term policies of arms sales to Taiwan and to work to reduce arms sales to the island gradually!

3- The action of the United States did not come randomly, nor was commercial profit from selling weapons to Taiwan intended by it. Rather, it wanted by it to pressure China to respond to it on several matters, among them raising the value of the Chinese currency against the dollar, and other trade matters, as well as the matter of censorship of the American electronic search engine “Google”, in which the American state intervened directly.

4- Moreover, China has begun to show international political work away from its surroundings, exploiting the shaking of America's international position because of America's financial crisis and its crisis in Iraq and Afghanistan. So America wanted to create an influential problem in China's neighbourhood, to occupy it with the Taiwan issue and heat it up after its temperature had frozen, or nearly... That is on the one hand. On the other hand, it is to be a message to China that America is strong and its international lustre has not yet been extinguished, besides being a message likewise to the other major states.

5- As for Taiwan's importance to America, it is nothing of consequence compared with America's interest that is achieved through its relationship with China. Since 1979 America has abandoned its recognition of Taiwan and acknowledged that People's China is the one that represents the people of China. And Obama added to these positions towards China other encouraging positions since he came to power, especially what he tried to show China with broad smiles during his last visit to China in November 2009 CE, when Obama in that visit welcomed China's global role and announced his intention to strengthen and develop relations, even the military ones... That is because America needs China in many matters, whether financial, commercial or in foreign policy...

6- All of this indicates that America cannot sacrifice its relations with China for the sake of 6.4 billion dollars, nor for the sake of Taiwan, which is worth nothing on the international political map, and which it has abandoned as a state representing the Chinese...

Therefore, the heating up of the atmosphere with China will not go beyond calculated means of pressure, especially since America is convinced that the Chinese reaction will not reach the point of a rupture in relations between them,

so much so that one of the American officials said recently: “China's reaction is temporary.”
